Pathway gene coexpression network from RNA-seq data

rna_network.Rd

Builds a gene coexpression network for genes belonging to a selected pathway using normalized RNA-seq expression data stored in the active rna_project.

The function translates pathway-level gene sets (from GSEA results) into a correlation-based network, where edges represent gene-gene coexpression within a defined experimental group.

Beyond network construction, the function supports two complementary analytical views:

  • Global structure (node_filter = "all"): preserves the full pathway topology, enabling interpretation of modular organization and overall connectivity.

  • Hub-centered structure (node_filter = "top"): restricts visualization to the most central genes, emphasizing regulatory influence and core network drivers.

These two modes represent different biological perspectives rather than simple visual filtering.

Usage

rna_network(
  project,
  pathway = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  threshold = 0.8,
  cor_p = 0.05,
  node_filter = c("all", "top"),
  top_nodes = 0.2,
  cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman", "auto"),
  community_method = c("louvain", "leiden", "none"),
  layout = c("fr", "kk", "stress", "lgl", "graphopt"),
  color_by = c("expression", "log2fc"),
  labels = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  plot = TRUE,
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

rna_project object created by rna_project().

pathway

Character or numeric. Pathway name or index from GSEA results.

group

Character. Experimental group used to compute correlations.

threshold

Numeric. Minimum absolute correlation required to define an edge.

cor_p

Numeric. Maximum p-value allowed for correlations.

node_filter

Character. Defines the structural view of the network:

  • "all": full pathway network (recommended for structural interpretation)

  • "top": restricted network containing only the most central genes

Important: When node_filter = "top", the network is no longer a full pathway graph but a centrality-enriched subnetwork, highlighting influential genes rather than full modular architecture.

top_nodes

Numeric. Fraction of most central nodes retained when node_filter = "top" (default: 0.2).

cor_method

Character. Correlation method used:

  • "pearson": linear coexpression structure

  • "spearman": rank-based robustness

  • "auto": adaptive choice based on sample size

community_method

Character. Community detection strategy:

  • "louvain": favors larger, coarse-grained modules (global view)

  • "leiden": more stable and fine-grained community structure

  • "none": no explicit modular partitioning

Guidance:

  • Use louvain for full-network interpretation (all)

  • Use leiden for hub-focused or reduced networks (top)

  • Use none when focusing on continuous gradients of connectivity

layout

Character. Graph layout algorithm:

  • "fr": fast global layout, good for overview plots

  • "kk": balanced structure-preserving layout

  • "stress": best preservation of relational distances (recommended for top nodes)

  • "lgl": scalable layout for larger networks

  • "graphopt": compact structure visualization

Guidance:

  • fr: publication-style overview of full networks

  • stress: best for interpreting hub-centered structures

  • kk: balanced exploratory analysis

color_by

Method used to color network nodes:

  • expression: colors nodes according to the z-scored mean expression of each gene across samples in the selected group.

  • log2fc: colors nodes according to the log2 fold change obtained from the current comparison stored in the project.

labels

Logical. Wheter to display gene labels in the network plot.

seed

Optional integer used for reproducibility.

plot

Logical. Whether to display the network plot.

save

Logical. Whether to store results in rna_project.

Value

An object of class "rna_network" containing:

params

List of parameters used to build the network

pathway

Selected pathway name

genes

Genes belonging to the pathway

graph

Network object from igraph

edges

Edge table with correlation statistics

nodes

Node table containing gene annotations, expression summaries, degree, betweenness centrality, harmonic centrality, community assignments, hub classification, and the composite hub score, where applicable.

The function invisibly returns a list containing:

  • result: the network object

  • project: updated project object (when save = TRUE)

Details

The function expects pre-computed GSEA results and normalized expression data.

The resulting network is sensitive to filtering choices:

  • Lower threshold increases connectivity and density

  • node_filter = "top" shifts interpretation toward central regulators

  • Community structure becomes less stable in highly filtered networks

Therefore, parameter selection should reflect the biological question:

Recommended usage patterns:

  • Pathway structure exploration: all + leiden + stress

  • Regulatory hub discovery: top + none/leiden + stress

  • Publication figure: all + louvain + fr

Interpretation note

Networks generated with node_filter = "top" represent a centrality-enriched projection of the pathway, not the full coexpression topology.

Network centrality

Network centrality is characterized using three complementary metrics:

  • Degree: number of direct connections, representing local connectivity.

  • Betweenness centrality: measures how frequently a node lies on shortest paths between other nodes, highlighting potential bridging positions in the network.

  • Harmonic centrality: quantifies node accessibility using the inverse of shortest-path distances to other nodes.

Harmonic centrality is used instead of conventional closeness centrality because pathway coexpression networks may contain disconnected components. Unlike conventional closeness centrality, harmonic centrality accounts for unreachable nodes by assigning them zero contribution, allowing comparisons across nodes in disconnected networks.

Shortest-path distances are derived from absolute correlation weights, such that stronger correlations correspond to shorter distances.

The hub_score is calculated as the sum of the standardized degree, betweenness centrality, and harmonic centrality values. It represents a composite exploratory measure of network centrality rather than a validated biological measure of regulatory influence.

Stored output

When save = TRUE, the network object is stored in:

rna_project$analyses$network

allowing reproducibility and downstream reuse.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

# Build network for top enriched pathway
rna_network(project = my_project)

# Use a specific pathway from GSEA
rna_network(my_project,
            pathway = 'Cellular Response To Starvation')

# Restrict labels to top 20% genes
rna_network(my_project,
            node_filter = 'top',
            top_nodes = 0.2)

# Use Spearman correlation
rna_network(my_project,
            cor_method = "spearman")

# Change layout algorithm
rna_network(my_project,
            layout = "stress")

} # }
